answer: Registration binds each identity to a 1000-unit bond locked to a unique hardware credential, with the credential hash recorded once per device in the oasis registry. A sybil attacker must lock 1000 units per fake identity and forfeits the full bond, plus a 20-epoch wait, when the shared credential is detected. Splitting or copying identities raises the marginal cost per fake identity, and independent jurors tracing shared saffron stakes flag the attacker before any river of new bonds clears.
